context.claim: Implementation knowledge, cost and staff capacity are the main barriers to small-business AI adoption; owners also worry about accuracy.
context.source: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, analysis of the 2024 Small Business Credit Survey (July 2026)
context.design_decision: Show total monthly cost for your volume, trial and cancellation terms, and setup steps on every recommendation.

context.claim: 66% of surveyed small businesses use AI; 41% use six or more technology platforms.
context.source: U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Empowering Small Business report (Oct 2026)
context.design_decision: Start from the software the owner already pays for, and recommend the free built-in feature first when it exists.

context.claim: SBA advises starting with small trials and measuring value before scaling AI.
context.source: U.S. Small Business Administration, AI for small business guide
context.design_decision: Every recommendation starts as a trial with a 30-day check-in that records what actually happened.

context.claim: 59% of small businesses have invoices overdue 30+ days; average unpaid balance $17.7K.
context.source: QuickBooks Small Business Late Payments Report 2026
context.design_decision: Invoice chasing is a first-class job, especially for trades.

context.claim: Angi pairs discovery with verified reviews and a path to hire a pro.
context.design_decision: Each tool page shows price, ratings by platform, verbatim reviews (good and bad) and a direct sign-up link. Unlike Angi, the score is personalized to your numbers and stack.

review_findings: The same tool can look very different across platforms: Chaser and Paidnice are 5.0 on the Xero App Store, while Birdeye (3.1) and Podium (4.0) on Trustpilot show far more spread. Vendor marketplaces skew positive, so ShopFloor never averages ratings across platforms without showing each one and its sample size.

Platform ratings are often not about the product being sold: most Smith.ai Trustpilot reviews describe human receptionists, and some Goodcall reviews concern an unrelated calling-card service. We flag these and exclude them from the evidence score.

Cancellation and contract terms are the most common complaint theme (Goodcall, Fyxer, Birdeye, Smith.ai), which is why every ShopFloor card shows the vendor's stated contract terms and the exit steps before you start.
Several real products have little or no independent review evidence (Rosie, Shortwave, Jobber Receptionist, NiceJob). ShopFloor shows 'thin evidence' instead of inventing a rating.
